Welcome to **GT 1000: First-Year Seminar, Physics**. This course is designed to help you make a successful transition to college by becoming better acquainted with the academic and social environments here at Georgia Tech.

Through the semester you will build strategies that promote academic, social, and professional success, learn how to navigate the resources available to you at Tech, and explore what it means to be a physicist at the undergraduate, graduate, and career levels. This is a highly interactive course that requires active student participation and working collaboratively in small groups.

## Course Description

This seminar course is designed to help you make a successful transition to college by becoming better acquainted with the academic and social environments here at Georgia Tech. Through the course, you will acquire strategies that promote academic, social, and professional success. This is a highly interactive course that requires active student participation and working collaboratively in small groups.

There are no prerequisites. This section is intended for first-year students in Physics, Astrophysics, and Applied Physics.

### Learning Outcomes

- Develop self-awareness and self-knowledge, particularly as it relates to academic interests and professional goals.
- Describe your path to graduation and identify opportunities for academic and professional enrichment with the assistance of a faculty member or advisor.
- Demonstrate the ability to lead and productively participate in collaborative projects.
- Be aware of what it means to be a physicist and explore opportunities for physicists at the undergraduate, graduate, and career levels.

## Assignments and Grading

There are no exams in this course. Your grade is based on participation and attendance together with the Team Project and two graded categories, Academic Planning and Career Readiness, each holding several smaller deliverables. All four components are weighted equally. Written assignments should be submitted on Canvas in PDF format by **11:59 PM ET** unless otherwise specified.

| Course Component | Due Date | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| Participation, short assignments, and attendance | Weekly | 25% |
| Team Project | TBD | 25% |
| Academic Planning | Multiple deliverables | 25% |
| Career Readiness | Multiple deliverables | 25% |

### Assignment Descriptions

- **Participation, short assignments, and attendance:** Attendance and active participation in each class session, along with short in-class and take-home assignments. Excessive lateness and absences (three or more per semester) can negatively impact your final grade.
- **[Team Project](assignments/team-project.qmd):** TBD.
- **[Academic Planning](assignments/academic-planning.qmd):** A category of several deliverables covering your path to graduation and academic enrichment. TBD.
- **[Career Readiness](assignments/career-readiness.qmd):** A category of several deliverables covering professional preparation. The first is your **résumé, due September 11**. TBD.

## A Few Important Course Notes

- **Attendance is mandatory.** This is a highly interactive course, and excessive lateness or absences (three or more per semester) can negatively impact your final grade. If you will miss class, please email the instructor as soon as possible.
- **Check your GT email and Canvas daily.** Important class announcements and information are posted to Canvas.
- **No textbook is required.** Course materials and assignment information will be provided through Canvas.
- **The use of generative AI is strongly discouraged.** This course is based in your own discovery, exploration, and reflection. Per the Georgia Tech Honor Code, no work produced via AI should be submitted as your own.
- **When in doubt, ask.** If you are unsure whether a resource, collaboration, or AI use is appropriate, contact the instructor before submitting.
